How this is computed: events come from Today's check-in (Present / Late / Call-out / No-show buttons). Points and occurrences apply the Policy builder settings, with decay and exempt categories. Click a row to see the full timeline.

Policy mode

Points-based rewards graduated severity (e.g. 3 callouts < 1 no-show). Occurrence-based counts incidents flatly. Hybrid tracks both and triggers on whichever is hit first — this is what most DSPs use.

Event types & severity

Set the point value and whether the event counts as an occurrence. Set zero points to disable scoring for that event.

Late arrival
Beyond grace period
Call-out
Notice given before threshold window
Early clock-out
Left route before completion without approval
No-call no-show
No notice, or notice within the threshold window
VTO — voluntary time off
Manager-offered opt-out (over-scheduled day). Default is 0 points / not an occurrence — never counts against the driver. Tracked separately so you can see if your cushion is too high.
PointsCounts as occ.

Windows & grace periods

Call-out window
Notice given at least this many hours before shift counts as call-out. Less = no-call no-show.
hours before shift
Late grace period
Arrivals within this window of scheduled start are not counted as late.
minutes
Decay / aging
Events older than this drop off the driver's running total.
days rolling
Reset cadence
Rolling = continuous decay. Quarterly = full reset on quarter boundary.

Schedule rules & compliance

The system enforces these automatically. Conflicts surface inline as you build the schedule.

Availability options

Allow drivers to manage their own availability
When ON, drivers see and edit availability in their app (subject to rules below). When OFF, only you set each driver's availability — drivers see their schedule but can't change what days they work.

Driver-managed mode is ON. Rules below apply to what drivers can declare in their app.

Operating days
Drivers can only declare availability for days you operate. Off days are hidden from the driver app.
Required days · all drivers must be available
Drivers cannot mark these days unavailable. Use sparingly — typically high-volume days.
Minimum days available per driver
Drivers must declare at least this many days as available (across operating days).
Maximum days unavailable per driver
Drivers can't mark more than this many operating days as unavailable.
Hours-per-week range allowed
Drivers can set their min/max hours within this range only.
to
Allow drivers to set "preferred" days
If off, drivers can only mark days as available or unavailable — no preference distinction.
Allow drivers to opt into backup pool
If off, you assign backup status manually. If on, drivers self-select.
Allow drivers to opt into swap marketplace
If off, drivers can't post or claim swaps — manager only.
Availability changes require owner approval
Driver edits stay pending until you approve. Useful for tighter control.
Availability change cutoff

Logic summary. RouteReady computes shift duration from clock-in/clock-out, active delivery time from first to last scan, and idle gap as their difference. Drivers with idle gap > 90 min are flagged High; 30–90 min Medium; < 30 min Low. Estimated excess hours = sum of idle gaps over the 90-min threshold.
